title: Building a Real-Time Crypto Dashboard: A Complete Walkthrough
subtitle: From websockets to charts — a practical, end-to-end guide.
excerpt: Learn how to build a live cryptocurrency dashboard with Django, websockets, and Chart.js — including data flow, code, and deployment tips.

content.introduction: Real-time dashboards feel like magic, but the building blocks are simple once you see them laid out. In this walkthrough we'll wire up a live crypto price dashboard step by step.

sections.title: What we're building
sections.content: A single-page dashboard that streams live prices for a handful of coins, updates charts in real time, and degrades gracefully when the connection drops.

sections.title: Tech stack
items: Django for the backend and templating
A websocket feed for live prices
Redis to fan out updates to connected clients

sections.title: Connecting to the price feed
sections.content:
import websocket, json

def on_message(ws, message):
    data = json.loads(message)
    print(data['symbol'], data['price'])

ws = websocket.WebSocketApp(
    'wss://stream.example.com/prices',
    on_message=on_message,
)
ws.run_forever()

sections.title: Heads up
sections.content: Always throttle chart re-renders. Updating on every single tick will pin the CPU on busy markets — batch updates every 500ms instead.

content.conclusion: That's the whole pipeline — a live feed, a fan-out layer, and a throttled UI. From here you can add more coins, historical charts, or price alerts. Happy building!
